links.outcome: Response consistency across three repeated runs of same radiograph (Fleiss' Kappa)
links.effect: Gemini 2.0 showed excellent reliability for large pneumothorax (Kappa = 1.00), while Claude 3.5 showed moderate consistency across both pneumothorax sizes.
links.quote: Regarding consistency, Gemini 2.0 demonstrated excellent reliability for large pneumothorax (Kappa = 1.00), while Claude 3.5 showed moderate consistency across both pneumothorax sizes.

links.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy by patient age group and pneumothorax size
links.effect: Adult overall accuracy: ChatGPT-4o 69.6%, Claude 3.5 64.9%, Gemini 2.0 57.4%; pediatric 20.8%, 12.5%, 20.8%. ChatGPT-4o large vs small pneumothorax 81.6% vs 42.2% (p<0.001).
links.quote: Performance was significantly poorer in pediatric patients across all models (20.8%, 12.5%, and 20.8%, respectively).

links.outcome: Performance in pediatric patients versus adults when applied outside validated population
links.effect: Overall accuracy in patients aged ≤12 years was 20.8%, 12.5%, and 20.8% versus 57.4-69.6% in adults across the three models.
links.quote: Performance was significantly poorer in pediatric patients across all models (20.8%, 12.5%, and 20.8%, respectively).

screen.reason: Retrospective benchmark evaluating diagnostic accuracy and consistency of three multimodal LLMs (GPT-4o, Gemini 2.0, Claude 3.5) on chest radiographs for pneumothorax detection without testing specific deployment safeguards.
